customer_question: The RFQ form was filled in as BR/EDR/BLE, but the module being used is BLE-only. Which scope should we register?
question_variants: The module is BLE-only but the product spec sheet says Bluetooth 5.0 — should we register BR/EDR as well?
We accidentally wrote BR/EDR/BLE on the RFQ. Does it need to be corrected?
actual_issue: The customer entered BR/EDR/BLE as the registration scope on the RFQ, but the actual Espressif module supports BLE only. Registration must match the device's actual implemented features — registering BR/EDR for a BLE-only module will cause ICS inconsistencies and block registration.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth certification is scoped to the features the product actually implements. BR/EDR and BLE use entirely different ICS items, test cases, and QDIDs. Attempting to include BR/EDR for a BLE-only module will generate Consistency Check errors that cannot be cleared. The RFQ entry must be corrected to BLE-only before proceeding.
consultant_answer: Since the module is BLE-only, the registration scope must be changed to BLE-only. The BR/EDR/BLE entry on the RFQ is incorrect and must be corrected.
decision_logic:
1. Confirm the module's Bluetooth feature set from its datasheet (BLE-only vs. Classic+BLE).
2. Register only the features the module actually supports.
3. If the RFQ entry is wrong, correct it before starting the provisional project — otherwise the ICS structure will be wrong from the beginning.
final_recommendation: When receiving an RFQ, always confirm the module's Bluetooth mode (BLE-only vs. Classic+BLE) from the datasheet. If unclear, ask the customer before building a provisional project.
risk_if_done_wrong: Building a provisional project with the wrong scope (BR/EDR for a BLE-only module) produces irreconcilable ICS errors and requires starting over.
